title: FAiT: Frequency-Aware Inverted Transformer for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

problem.claim: Transformer self-attention in multivariate time series forecasting smooths high-frequency signals needed for sharp local changes.

gap.claim: Existing frequency-domain designs commonly use fixed spectral bases and uniform sequence-wise modulation, which does not account for time-varying spectral characteristics.

contributions.claim: FAiT uses Inverted Attention to construct a complementary high-pass branch by inverting the attention matrix and recover attenuated transient signals.
FAiT introduces Dynamic Temporal-Frequency Modulation to generate instance-conditioned weights that adaptively recalibrate spectral sub-band energy.
FAiT is designed to provide fine-grained control over evolving multi-scale temporal patterns while maintaining computational efficiency.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on widely used benchmarks reportedly show that FAiT consistently outperforms state-of-the-art Transformer-based and frequency-enhanced baselines.
The authors report that FAiT maintains computational efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Transformer self-attention is described as a low-pass filter that suppresses high-frequency signals relevant to sharp local changes.
Existing frequency-domain approaches are described as relying on fixed spectral bases and uniform modulation despite evolving spectral characteristics.
FAiT addresses the limitation with Inverted Attention and a complementary high-pass branch for recovering attenuated transient signals.
Dynamic Temporal-Frequency Modulation adaptively recalibrates spectral sub-band energy using instance-conditioned weights.
Benchmark experiments reportedly show improved performance over stated baselines with computational efficiency.
